cards.label: InjectionShield-Lite v2: new attack styles
cards.detail: Roman Urdu recall, v1 → v2 (v2 trained on similar styles; optimistic)

findings.title: D1: detection rate by language
findings.statement: ProtectAI DeBERTa-v3 (v2) detected 89.8% (95% CI 85.5–94.0%) of English attacks but 61.0% (95% CI 52.0–70.0%) of Roman Urdu attacks. The confidence intervals do not overlap. Paired test on the same prompts: McNemar p < 0.001.

findings.title: D2: detection rate by language
findings.statement: English-only baseline detected 92.8% (95% CI 89.2–96.4%) of English attacks but 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–0.0%) of Urdu (script) attacks. The confidence intervals do not overlap. Paired test on the same prompts: McNemar p < 0.001.

findings.title: D1: language-switch bypass
findings.statement: Of the attacks caught in English by ProtectAI DeBERTa-v3 (v2), 36.3% (95% CI 26.1–46.2%) were missed when the same attack was written in Roman Urdu (33 of 91 attacks).

findings.title: D2: language-switch bypass
findings.statement: Of the attacks caught in English by English-only baseline, 100.0% (95% CI 100.0–100.0%) were missed when the same attack was written in Urdu (script) (152 of 152 attacks).

findings.title: D1: false alarms on harmless text
findings.statement: ProtectAI DeBERTa-v3 (v2) wrongly flagged 0.6% of harmless English prompts and 88.6% (95% CI 83.2–93.4%) of harmless Urdu (script) prompts (highest false-positive rate across languages).

findings.title: D2: false alarms on harmless text
findings.statement: English-only baseline wrongly flagged 0.6% of harmless English prompts and 5.0% (95% CI 1.0–9.0%) of harmless Roman Urdu prompts (highest false-positive rate across languages).

findings.title: D1: blanket flagging of Urdu (script)
findings.statement: ProtectAI DeBERTa-v3 (v2)'s 95.7% recall on Urdu (script) is not a sign of robustness: it also flagged 88.6% of harmless Urdu (script) prompts (ROC-AUC 0.70), i.e. it flags most text in this language regardless of content.

findings.title: Multilingual embeddings: what transfers without Urdu data
findings.statement: Multilingual MiniLM embeddings trained on English only (A2): Urdu (script) recall 94.5% / FPR 7.8%; Roman Urdu recall 77.0% / FPR 58.0%. Trained on multilingual data (D4): Urdu (script) recall 92.1% / FPR 2.4%; Roman Urdu recall 70.0% / FPR 20.0%. Roman Urdu was the lowest-F1 language for 6 of 8 detectors (D1, D3, D4, D3v2, D4v2, A2).

findings.title: D3: InjectionShield-Lite vs the English-only baseline
findings.statement: Recall, English-only baseline → InjectionShield-Lite: Urdu (script) 0.0% → 93.3%; Roman Urdu 34.0% → 80.0%; Urdu-English code-mixed 90.0% → 90.0% (CIs overlap). InjectionShield-Lite's lowest recall was 80.0% (Roman Urdu) with false-positive rates between 0.0% and 2.0%. Caveat: its Roman Urdu / code-mixed training and test rows were written by the same (LLM) author, which may flatter these numbers.

findings.title: Ablation: features vs training data
findings.statement: Recall for word n-grams (English data) / char n-grams (English data) / char n-grams (multilingual data) — Urdu (script): 0.0% / 0.0% / 93.3%; Roman Urdu: 34.0% / 29.0% / 80.0%; Urdu-English code-mixed: 90.0% / 89.0% / 90.0%. The first step shows what character features alone contribute; the second shows what multilingual training data adds.

findings.title: Generalisation to unseen attack styles
findings.statement: On 100 Roman Urdu and 100 Urdu-script attacks phrased in new styles (fake authority, developer modes, role-play; supplied after training, attack-only), recall Roman Urdu / Urdu was: D1 92.0% / 98.0%; D2 45.0% / 0.0%; D3 41.0% / 38.0%; D4 62.0% / 69.0%. InjectionShield-Lite's benchmark Roman Urdu recall (80.0%) does not carry over to these unseen attack styles: it mostly learned the attack patterns present in its training data. The multilingual-embedding models (D4, A2) generalised better. ProtectAI's high Urdu recall should be read together with its false-positive rate on harmless Urdu.

findings.title: D3v2: retraining for new attack styles
findings.statement: InjectionShield-Lite v2 adds training data covering these attack styles and look-alike harmless prompts. Stress-set recall (Roman Urdu / Urdu) rose from 41.0% / 38.0% to 79.0% / 72.0%. This is optimistic, because the extra data was written after the stress-set categories were known (no sentence was allowed to be similar to a stress-set item). On 150 English and 150 Urdu fresh real-user harmless prompts that mention words like system, developer, instructions or access, the false-positive rate (English / Urdu) was 7.3% / 4.0% for v1 and 4.0% / 7.3% for v2. Benchmark Roman Urdu recall: 85.0% (FPR 1.0%).

findings.title: D1: false alarms confirmed on independently written Urdu
findings.statement: On 35 harmless Urdu-script sentences written independently of the benchmark (supplied after training), ProtectAI DeBERTa-v3 (v2) flagged 35 (100.0%) as attacks.

note: All statements are generated automatically from results/metrics.json. Test-set sizes are small (about 330 prompts in English/Urdu, 200 in Roman Urdu/code-mixed), so confidence intervals are wide.
